name: A Dataset for Answering Time-Sensitive Questions
description: Time is an important dimension in our physical world. Lots of facts can evolve with respect to time. For example, the U.S. President might change every four years. Therefore, it is important to consider the time dimension and empower the existing QA models to reason over time. However, the existing QA datasets contain rather few time-sensitive questions, hence not suitable for diagnosing or benchmarking the model's temporal reasoning capability. In order to promote research in this direction, we propose to construct a time-sensitive QA dataset. The dataset is constructed by 1) mining time-evolving facts from WikiData and aligning them to their corresponding Wikipedia page, 2) employing crowd workers to verify and calibrate these noisy facts, 3) generating question-answer pairs based on the annotated time-sensitive facts. reputation: A niche temporal QA dataset used to study time-sensitive reasoning, but not as widely adopted as major QA benchmarks.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark centered on temporal reasoning over evolving facts; results can be sensitive to temporal leakage and dataset construction noise.
